newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Soccer-French group wins African Cup rights.
newsitem.headline: Soccer-French group wins African Cup rights.

text.p: French marketing firm Mediafoot and the television station Canal France International have been awarded the rights to next year's African Champions' League, the Confederation of African Football (CAF) confirmed on Sunday.
The joint bid for the publicity and television rights to the 24 matches in the Champions' League will cost $3 million.
"They wanted to sign for a longer period but we were not happy to do this just yet," said CAF press officer Viken Djizmedjian on Sunday.
"We also still have some minor details to work out," he added.

CAF have introduced the Champions' League in a bid to generate revnue for participating clubs and itself. A total of 70 percent will be divided up among the eight participating clubs with the rest going to the Cairo-based confederation.
The French bid beat off similiar offers from the US-based International Management Group (IMG), who have been making a strong play in international soccer over the last year, and the Swiss-based ISL.
"IMG also offered us $3 million but they placed too many conditions on the offer," Djizmedjian said.
The Champions' League will start in September after the annual African Champions' Cup has reached the quarter-final stages.
The eight remaining teams will be divided into two groups of four with the group winners decided on a home-and-away league system.
The group winners will meet in the two-leg final in December next year.
Mediafoot already hold existing rights to all of the Confederation of African Football's cup finals and the biennial African Nations' Cup finals, until the turn of the century.
The French firm, which was recently listed on the Paris bourse, also holds rights to the 1998 World Cup finals in France.
